stories.body: More than 550,000 people demonstrated across France on Saturday over the cost of living, weak public services and conditions in secondary schools. Most marches were peaceful, but violent groups set fires, looted businesses and attacked public buildings in several cities. Authorities said more than 1,200 people were arrested and 150 police officers were injured; fires badly damaged Limoges town hall and a tourist office in Lyon.
stories.headline: Violence erupts across France during protests over living costs and schools

stories.body: Masked Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and clergy visiting Taybeh in the occupied West Bank during the olive harvest, damaging a Belgian diplomatic vehicle and injuring several people. Belgium called on Israel to prosecute those responsible, while the Israeli military and foreign minister condemned the attack and said it was being investigated. The incident followed another settler assault that injured Palestinians and a Washington Post photographer.
stories.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomatic delegation in the West Bank

stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two tankers carrying about two million barrels of crude each caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian media said the vessels had disabled their tracking and radar systems and used an unauthorised route. The claimed attacks come amid a sharp escalation around the waterway, where disruptions have cut oil flows and raised energy prices.
stories.headline: Iran says two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: The United Arab Emirates has reportedly agreed to resume payments to southern Yemeni forces fighting the Houthis, while Saudi Arabia will provide air cover. The arrangement signals limited repair of a Saudi-Emirati split over Yemen as Houthi advances and attacks on Saudi infrastructure alarm Gulf governments. Saudi-led forces also said they intercepted four drones over Riyadh and other regions.
stories.headline: UAE agrees to resume support for Yemeni forces amid Houthi gains

stories.body: Canadian officials confirmed deaths and injuries after a serious incident caused a major fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta. Strong winds pushed the fire beyond the base perimeter, prompting a multi-agency response. Defence Minister David McGuinty did not give casualty numbers or identify the cause, describing the situation as active and delicate.
stories.headline: Deaths confirmed after major fire at Canadian military base

stories.body: Republican candidates are largely avoiding Donald Trump in their advertising even as he holds rallies to mobilise his base. Democrats and allied groups have spent far more on ads mentioning Trump, while several Republican candidates in competitive races have sought distance from his Iran policy, tariffs and low approval ratings. Trump aides say they are allowing vulnerable candidates latitude while using rallies to boost turnout among MAGA voters.
stories.headline: Republicans distance campaign advertising from Trump before midterms

stories.body: Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces an unexpectedly competitive Kansas race against Democrat Adam Hamilton, a United Methodist pastor. National party groups are spending millions to support Marshall, but critics within his party say he began campaigning too late and took the state for granted. The contest has also been shaped by voter anger over fuel prices, tariffs and immigration enforcement, as well as scrutiny of Marshall's campaign and personal ties to Kansas.
stories.headline: Kansas Senate race becomes a serious Republican liability

stories.body: Demonstrators gathered in Atlanta for a No Kings, Vote Now rally, one of several events held across the United States. Participants criticised President Donald Trump's policies, while organisers said the immediate aim was to encourage voting in the November 3 midterm elections and defend democratic institutions.
stories.headline: Atlanta No Kings rally urges turnout ahead of midterms

stories.body: Spain's main parties are moving into campaign mode ahead of the November 29 general election. Pedro Sánchez sought to energise Socialist supporters in Fuenlabrada, promising to protect pensions and highlighting the housing crisis; he also made a public declaration of support for his wife, Begoña Gómez. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo said he was prepared to govern with Vox, arguing that such coalitions already operate in several regional governments.
stories.headline: Spain's major parties set their election strategies

stories.body: Frente Amplio, the alliance of several left-wing parties including Sumar, Izquierda Unida, Comuns and Más Madrid, has abandoned efforts to reach a joint electoral agreement with Podemos. Both sides blamed the other for the failed negotiations, though their leaders called for voters on the left to mobilise. Podemos will run in Catalonia with ERC and Gabriel Rufián.
stories.headline: Spain's alternative left will run on separate electoral lists

stories.body: PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has called on the government to deploy the navy, summon Morocco's ambassador and demand explanations after Moroccan vessels entered Spanish waters near Ceuta during a summer migration incident. Defence authorities have reportedly tightened surveillance procedures, deploying patrol vessels near Ceuta and Melilla rather than waiting for ships to enter territorial waters.
stories.headline: Feijóo calls for a naval response to Moroccan vessels near Ceuta

stories.body: Spain's weather agency has issued red alerts for heavy rain, storms, wind and coastal conditions in Valencia as Storm Adam brings severe weather to much of the Mediterranean coast. Forecasts warn that Ibiza, Formentera, Valencia and northern Alicante could receive more than 300 litres of rain per square metre in 24 hours, with flooding and sudden rises in streams possible. Orange and yellow alerts are also in place in several other regions.
stories.headline: Storm Adam brings torrential-rain warnings across Spain's Mediterranean coast

stories.body: Torrential rain from Storm Adam temporarily halted operations at Barcelona-El Prat airport, causing delays and cancellations, while emergency crews searched for a woman swept into a swollen stream in Cabrera de Mar. Authorities sent mobile emergency alerts across several Barcelona-area counties, suspended part of the R2 South commuter rail service and diverted regional trains. Heavy rain also led to rescues from vehicles and widespread disruption elsewhere in Catalonia.
stories.headline: Storm disrupts Barcelona airport as search continues for woman near Cabrera de Mar

stories.body: TMB installed temporary flood barriers at an entrance to the L9S Parc Logístic station as heavy rain approached Barcelona. The plastic L-shaped barriers are intended to redirect water and protect the station, which was affected by flooding earlier this month. TMB is evaluating the pilot before buying barriers for use at other stations, while continuing to rely on measures such as sandbags in the meantime.
stories.headline: Barcelona Metro trials flood barriers at Parc Logístic station

stories.body: Badalona mayor Xavier García Albiol will head the People's Party list in Barcelona for Spain's November 29 general election. Albiol said he would remain mayor while bringing his priorities on illegal occupations, repeat offending and irregular immigration to Congress. The announcement comes before Alberto Núñez Feijóo's planned pre-campaign event in Barcelona.
stories.headline: Xavier García Albiol will lead the PP's Barcelona ticket
